title: A Method for Growing Bio-memristors from Slime Mold
protocol: Load a 3D printer with High-Impact Polystyrene (HIPS) by setting the print bed temperature to 85 °C and the extruder to 230 °C.
Loosen the idler arm, insert the filament, and push down until it starts to extrude out of the hot end.
Retighten the filament idler arm and remove the extruded material.
Import the 3D receptacle STL model file into a 3D printing slicing software by navigating to the file tab and selecting the import/open options.
Select high quality print settings in the slicing software while ensuring that the correct material profile is selected.
Set the software to print each object one at a time if printing several receptacles in one run.
Wait until the print bed temperature is below 50 °C before removing the printed parts.
Gently clear the electrode socket of any imperfections with a thin wire brush to prevent obstructions when fitting the chamber with an electrode.
Replace the HIPS filament for a cleaning filament and run plenty of the material through the print head.
Load an electrically conductive polylactic acid (PLA) filament with a volume resistivity of 0.75 Ω-cm or less into the printer.
Set the print bed temperature to 60 °C and the extruder temperature to 230 °C.
Extrude several centimeters of filament through the print head when temperatures are reached to remove particulates from previous sessions.
Using a 3D printing slicing software, load the electrode STL file.
Specify layer height = 0.16 mm, shell thickness = 1.7 mm, bottom/top thickness = 0.74 mm, and fill density = 100% in print settings.
Set the printer to print one electrode at a time if printing multiple electrodes.
Leave printed electrodes on the print bed until they cool to room temperature.
Slot an electrode into each of the two chambers.
Cut a 10 mm piece of Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) tubing with a 4 mm inner diameter and 6 mm outer diameter using a sharp scalpel, ensuring both ends are straight and clean.
Gently ease each end of the PVC tubing over the rim of the two electrodes.
Put 2 g of non-nutrient microbiological agar powder into a 250 mL glass bottle.
Add 100 mL of deionized water and mix well.
Autoclave the bottle for 12 - 15 min at 121 °C or place in a boiling water bath for 15 - 20 min.
Melt the agar using a water bath or microwave.
Fill a 2 mL pipette with molten agar.
Hover the nib of the pipette approximately 5 mm above the internal base of each receptacle's chamber and slowly fill the wells up to the bottom of the connecting tube hole.
Place a lid on each of the chambers immediately after filling the wells.
Set the receptacle aside until the agar has set and reached room temperature.
Place an oat flake in each of the two chambers.
Remove one 2 mL blob of pseudopods from a starved (approximately 12 h) culture of plasmodium.
Place the protoplasm in one of the two chambers containing an oat flake.
